build.summary: Built found-lab-controls-registry. The table-side controls are now a strip of tabs found by glob, and every tab talks to the lab through one lab-agnostic LabControlsTarget, which DiagnosticLabSession implements. The four existing sections (C-arm and table, Imaging, Back table, Patient) moved into tab files with their markup unchanged. The foot switches, Inject, Aspirate and Store fluoro stay in the bar above the tabs. A one-off scratchpad check rendered the old component (from the snapshot) and the new one for all four tabs in two lab states, and the server-rendered HTML was byte-identical.

acceptance.criterion: Design: LabControlsTarget (C-arm, table, imaging, back table, defibrillator, plus optional capabilities queried by tabs); ControlTab { id, label, order, labs, visible(target, policy), Component }; registry globs tabs/*.tsx; DiagnosticLabSession implements LabControlsTarget; behaviour unchanged
acceptance.evidence: types.ts defines LabControlsTarget, ControlTab (visible is optional and defaults to shown), ControlTabProps and ControlKit. Optional capabilities are queried with capability(k); later packages add keys to LabCapabilities by module augmentation and register them with provideCapability, and 'patient' (the PatientEngine) is provided now. registry.ts uses import.meta.glob('./tabs/*.tsx', {eager:true}). The session declares 'implements LabControlsTarget'. Simulator.tsx still passes session={session} and typechecks. The session tests cover subscribeControls (re-renders on the same store slices the old useSim selectors watched, plus session notifications, and stops after dispose) and the setters (same store actions; values the lab does not offer are refused).

outOfScope: The Hold and Seg controls are shared by the shell and the tabs, and the file list has no file to hold them. TableSideControls.tsx defines them and passes them to every tab as the ControlKit prop, so tabs never import from the shell and there is no circular import. A small src/ui/lab/controls/kit.tsx would be a cleaner home if a later package's list allows it. No change is needed now.
build.notes:
Snapshot and the .started marker are in datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/found-lab-controls-registry/. The snapshot holds the three listed files that already existed: TableSideControls.tsx, labSession.ts and lab.test.ts. The other six listed files are new.

How it fits together:
- src/ui/lab/controls/types.ts defines the interfaces. LabControlsTarget is flat: the C-arm, table and memories; the imagingControls() read-out, including the field and rate options the lab offers, so the PCI lab can add 3.75 p/s without touching the tab; the back table; breath-hold and the defibrillator; subscribeControls, controlsVersion and controlsPolicy.
- src/ui/lab/controls/registry.ts exports collectControlTabs(modules) (checks each tab, sorts by order then id), CONTROL_TABS (the glob), and tabsFor(target, policy, tabs), which filters by the target's controlsLab and the tab's visible().
- A tab file exports `tab: ControlTab`. The core orders are 10, 20, 30 and 40. Back table is for the diagnostic lab only; the C-arm, Imaging and Patient tabs list both labs.
- TableSideControls keeps its props (session, input) and adds optional `tabs` and `initialTab`. If the open tab hides itself, the first tab shown takes its place.
- DiagnosticLabSession now:
  - declares controlsLab = 'diagnostic';
  - subscribes once to the store and bumps a counter only when imaging, cArm, pedal, catheterId, fluoroOn or policy changes (the same slices the old component selected), then calls the controls listeners;
  - folds its own notify() into controlsVersion();
  - adds thin wrappers over the existing store actions;
  - exports DIAGNOSTIC_FIELDS and DIAGNOSTIC_RATES.
  The store subscription is removed on dispose.
- No shared engine defaults changed. No doses, thresholds or device dimensions were added. All UI text is the old text, moved without change.
- Test fixtures are under src/ui/lab/controls/__fixtures__/tabs/, following the __fixtures__ convention of practiceIndex. They are not globbed by the runtime registry or picked up by vitest's include, which only matches *.test.ts. They do typecheck.
- Nothing was checked in the browser, as instructed; a separate stage checks the app.

review.verdict: PASS with minor findings. The design is implemented completely and behaviour is unchanged. types.ts defines LabControlsTarget, ControlTab { id, label, order, labs, visible?, Component } and LabCapabilities, which later packages extend by module augmentation. registry.ts globs ./tabs/*.tsx eagerly, validates each tab and sorts by order then id. The four sections moved into CArmTab, ImagingTab, BackTableTab and DefibTab (id 'patient'), and their markup matches the snapshot line for line. The foot switches, Inject, Aspirate and Store fluoro stay in the bar above the tabs. DiagnosticLabSession declares 'implements LabControlsTarget'. Its new store subscription watches the same slices the old useSim selectors watched (imaging, cArm, pedal, catheterId, fluoroOn) plus policy, and it is pushed to unsub, so dispose removes it. The setters call the same store actions as before. DIAGNOSTIC_FIELDS (25/20/16/12) and DIAGNOSTIC_RATES (7.5/15/30) are the old UI constants moved into the session, so no clinical numbers are new. lab.test.ts is byte-identical to its snapshot (empty diff), and integration.test.ts was not touched. I ran npx vitest run on controls.test.ts, lab.test.ts and integration.test.ts: 3 files, 31 tests passed. npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit is now clean; the 8 errors the builder saw in another package's files are gone. Files under src/ changed after .started that are not in this package's list all belong to other packages. src/state/useLabHandoverStore.ts and src/simulation/session/handover(.test).ts belong to found-handover-contract. src/simulation/patient/contrastBudget.test.ts, src/simulation/patient/patient.test.ts and src/simulation/team/formulary.test.ts belong to found-patient-formulary. The only new files outside the list are the test and its fixtures, as allowed. Simulator.tsx is the only consumer of TableSideControls, and its props still fit. There is no ground truth on screen: the UI text is the old text moved unchanged. The design system classes are unchanged and the new comments are in British English. The plan sets no tip integration or lesson links for this package, so neither is expected. No render-path per-frame allocations were added beyond the old component's own. tabsFor and imagingControls/backTable allocate small arrays and objects on each React render, at the same rate the old component re-rendered.

findings.where: src/ui/lab/controls/controls.test.ts, test 'stops listening to the store when disposed'
findings.problem: The test cannot fail. dispose() clears controlsListeners whether or not the store subscription was removed, so n stays 0 even if the store.subscribe unsub were never pushed. A leaked store subscription would pin the disposed session (and its engine) to the global store for good, and this test would not catch it.
findings.fix: Assert on the session's own counter instead of the listener: `const v = session.controlsVersion(); session.dispose(); g().setField(16); expect(session.controlsVersion()).toBe(v);` controlsRev only moves if the store listener is still attached. The n === 0 check can stay as well.

problems.where: C-arm and table tab, Centre button (target.table.set({x:0,y:0})), and the X key in src/ui/sim/Simulator.tsx:180; sync in DiagnosticLabSession.step, src/ui/sim/labSession.ts around line 663
problems.problem: Centre resets TableDrive to x=0, y=0, but the store pan is never updated. TableDrive.step() returns false when the table is at rest, because 'before' is taken after set(), so st0.setPan is never called. Observed: drive state {x:0,y:0} while the store imaging stayed at panX 0, panY 98.8 through several seconds of stepping. The image and readout stay off-centre. The snapshot has the same handler, so this bug was there before this package and does not break 'behaviour unchanged'.
problems.fix: In DiagnosticLabSession, wrap the table the controls get so that set() also writes the store. For example, add to the session: centreTable or override via a TableControl adapter: `readonly table` stays the TableDrive, and step() syncs whenever the drive and store differ: replace `if (this.table.step(dt)) {...}` with `const moved = this.table.step(dt); const ts = this.table.state; if (moved || ts.x !== st0.imaging.panX || ts.y !== st0.imaging.panY || ts.height !== st0.imaging.tableHeight) { st0.setPan(ts.x, ts.y); if (ts.height !== st0.imaging.tableHeight) st0.setTableHeight(ts.height); }`. This is in labSession.ts, which is in this package's file list. Since the package requires behaviour unchanged, it could go to a follow-up instead.

fix2.notes:
Both findings checked against the code and applied.

1. Tab strip overflow, in /Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator/src/ui/lab/TableSideControls.tsx. The finding was correct. The tablist was "flex border-b border-line px-1": it neither wraps nor scrolls, and it sits inside a panel with overflow hidden, so any tab past the panel width could not be reached. The tablist is now "flex overflow-x-auto border-b border-line px-1" and each tab button has shrink-0. Server-rendered HTML now differs from the old snapshot only by these two classes.

2. Centre leaves the image off-centre, in /Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator/src/ui/sim/labSession.ts, DiagnosticLabSession.step. The finding was correct. TableDrive.set() moves the drive and zeroes its velocity. step() then takes its 'before' snapshot after that move and returns false, so st0.setPan was never called. The store's panX/panY, which FluoroView and the readout use, stayed where they were. step() now syncs the store whenever the drive and the store differ, not only when the drive moved during that frame. Before applying it I confirmed that nothing else in src writes the store's pan or table height (setPan, panTable, centreTable and setTableHeight have no callers outside the store except this sync), and that the store's clamps (±90, ±120) match TableDrive's limits. So the drive is the only source and the sync cannot override another control or keep rewriting every frame. This also fixes the X key in Simulator.tsx, which calls the same session.table.set; that file was not edited. The bug predates this package, but the fix is in a listed file and only adds the missing store write, so I applied it here rather than deferring it.

Test added to /Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator/src/ui/lab/controls/controls.test.ts ('table centre'). It drives the table off-centre, releases it, calls table.set({x:0,y:0}), steps once, and checks that the store's panX and panY are 0. Nothing outside the package's files was touched.
